tasks.gr6-water-pollution-wetlands-t2: Topic: Water pollution and wetlands. Cover insoluble pollutants (oil, plastics, tyres, tins, glass, toilet waste), soluble pollutants (soaps, fertilizers, insecticides, acids, poisons), germs from toilet waste causing water-borne illnesses such as diarrhoea, and why wetlands matter (they remove substances, act like sponges, support biodiversity). Keep wording plain and gentle. Ask Grade 6 learners to sort pollutants and explain what a wetland does.
tasks.gr6-purifying-water-t2: Topic: Purifying dirty water. Cover sieving, settling, decanting, filtering, boiling and adding chemicals to kill germs, the layers of a sand filter (finest on top), municipal water being cleaned before and after use, and that water cleaned in a class experiment must not be drunk. Ask Grade 6 learners to order the steps and say which step removes which kind of thing.
tasks.gr6-rates-of-dissolving-t2: Topic: Rates of dissolving. Cover the three factors that change the time taken to dissolve (temperature, stirring or shaking, grain size), reading and comparing bar graphs of dissolving times (shorter bar is a faster rate), and a fair test that changes one thing and keeps the same amount of solute (for example 5 ml) and water (for example 125 ml). Ask Grade 6 learners to compare times, say which test is fair, and name what to keep the same.
